revision: Four paired situations; independent frequency ratings and one first approach per situation

D.name: Direction
D.focus: taking initiative, making decisions, and addressing challenges
D.question: Where would a clear decision help you move something forward?

I.name: Interaction
I.focus: starting conversations, sharing ideas, and involving people
I.question: Who would benefit from hearing your ideas or encouragement?

S.name: Steadiness
S.focus: maintaining a steady pace, listening, and following through
S.question: Which routine helps you give people dependable support?

C.name: Precision
C.focus: checking details, using criteria, and working through information
C.question: Where would clearer information make your next step easier?

options.D: decide on a next step and move toward a result
options.I: bring people into discussion to build momentum
options.S: keep progress moving at a measured, sustainable pace
options.C: review the criteria and assumptions before deciding

adapted.stem: When a work task is waiting for a decision

options.D: I choose a practical next action and get it underway
options.I: I get the people involved talking so we can build momentum
options.S: I keep the work moving steadily while the decision takes shape
options.C: I check the decision criteria and underlying assumptions

options.D: reset priorities and act on the new direction
options.I: talk with those involved and rally them around the change
options.S: restore a dependable rhythm amid the disruption
options.C: identify implications and adjust the plan carefully

adapted.stem: When priorities change unexpectedly during my workday

options.D: I redirect my effort toward the new objective
options.I: I discuss the change with colleagues and build support for it
options.S: I establish a workable routine around the revised plan
options.C: I trace what the change affects before adjusting the work

options.D: clarify objectives and establish where I can take charge
options.I: introduce myself widely and start conversations
options.S: learn the group rhythm and contribute consistently
options.C: understand its expectations, roles, and procedures

adapted.stem: When I start working with an unfamiliar team

options.D: I establish the goals and identify where I can take the lead
options.I: I introduce myself and open conversations with team members
options.S: I observe the working rhythm and settle into a consistent contribution
options.C: I find out how responsibilities, procedures, and expectations are defined

items.stem: When I accept responsibility for something

options.D: take ownership of the outcome and drive toward it
options.I: serve as an active connector among those involved
options.C: establish quality checks and completion criteria

adapted.stem: When a piece of work becomes my responsibility

options.D: I take charge of delivering the outcome
options.I: I keep the people involved connected and communicating
options.S: I provide consistent follow-through from day to day
options.C: I set checks for quality and define what completion looks like
